text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: elevated 504/timeout errors on dedicated pool vermilion-vpc-prod (customer: Vermilion Labs). 5m avg timeout rate 12%. Paging on-call.
Alex Reyes: ack. looking at ingress + router logs. tagging @Priya for kernel/kv cache visibility.
Priya Nair: I'm on it. I see a sharp rise in streaming session count from tenant_id=vermilion-labs starting ~09:08 UTC. KV-cache miss rate spiked and we started thrashing GPU memory on node a2-08-11.
Jamal Khan: do we have evidence it's tenant-isolated vs pool-wide?
Priya Nair: filtered by tenant -> ~84% of timeouts originate from vermilion-labs sessions. Other tenants stable. seems noisy-tenant.
Linh Tran (CSE): Vermilion support channel reporting many timed-out generation calls in-app. They're seeing retries which amplify load. asking for ETA.
Alex Reyes: immediate action: enable session cap and exponential backoff at edge for vermilion-labs, set cap=6 concurrent sessions per tenant, 30s idle timeout. applying now.
IncidentBot: Router: per-tenant session cap enabled for tenant=vermilion-labs by Alex Reyes.
Priya Nair: applying node cordon on a2-08-11 and will drain affected pods to reduce kernel pressure. command: ```kubectl cordon a2-08-11 && kubectl drain a2-08-11 --ignore-daemonsets --grace-period=30```
Jamal Khan: I'll spin up two spare nodes and rebalance to avoid noisy neighbor impact. launching autoscaler request.
Hannah Park (Billing): CS asked about SLA credits. we should capture impact window precisely. Linh, can you note the customer-facing timestamps?
Linh Tran (CSE): told Vermilion: "We're investigating — ETA ~20-30m." I'll update them after we have mitigation.
Priya Nair: quick post-mortem notes: cause appears to be a combination of (1) sudden surge in long-running streaming sessions from Vermilion, (2) an edge retry loop due to client timeouts, (3) a fallback quantized kernel path that allocates additional buffers leading to memory pressure on older GPUs.
Alex Reyes: temporary workaround: throttle session creation, route new requests to a light-weight non-streaming endpoint we control (vermilion-lite), and enable fallback 1 (less-quant aggressive) for existing in-flight sessions. Doing that now.
IncidentBot: DeployBot: rollback of quant-kernel tweak (rollout 2026-03-04-quant-fallback) initiated on vermilion-vpc-prod by Alex Reyes.
Jamal Khan: after draining node and caps, timeout rate dropped from 12% -> 0.9% over 8 minutes. KV miss rate stabilized.
Linh Tran (CSE): Vermilion engineering says their retry logic was aggressive; they've paused client retries on our ask. they want a short explanation for their CTO.
Hannah Park (Billing): propose goodwill credit: either 15% of impacted window usage or a flat $Xk credit. recommend we propose percentage first and loop billing for approval.
Priya Nair: telemetry shows 88% of failed requests were tied to streaming endpoints with >2k token context. We reproduced in staging with their sample workload. I've created repro runbook and captured traces in S3: s3://redwood-incidents/vermilion/trace-2634509876/
Alex Reyes: I'll own the ops follow-ups: extend watchdog to auto-throttle when per-tenant concurrent sessions > threshold and implement a circuit-breaker on kernel selection for known risky inputs.
Jamal Khan: devs: please add a defensive limit in runtime: if quantized kernel allocation would exceed N% of free GPU mem, fall back to safe kernel. Priya, can you draft the patch?
Priya Nair: yes, drafted a patch and test vectors. PR #902 in runtime-quant repo. scheduling a canary rollout to a non-prod pool overnight.
Linh Tran (CSE): DRAFT CUSTOMER NOTE -> "Hi Vermilion team, we observed increased timeout/errors impacting your dedicated pool from 09:089:22 UTC. We applied emergency session capping, routed traffic to a lighter endpoint, drained affected nodes, and rolled back a recent kernel tweak. Service normalized at 09:22 UTC. Root cause: a burst of long-lived streaming sessions combined with retries and an edge-case in our quantized kernel which increased memory allocations. We're preparing a full RCA and a patch; propose a goodwill credit for impacted usage. Linh / Redwood CSE"
Alex Reyes: remove any language that could sound blaming the customer. suggest: "originating from your workload patterns" and include concrete short-term mitigations for them: 1) pause client-side aggressive retries, 2) reduce max concurrent streams to 6, 3) share sample payloads for joint staging test.
Hannah Park (Billing): for credits propose 15% of the usage during impacted minute window and offer 30 days of enhanced support + one post-incident joint testing session free. I'll verify finance OK.
Jamal Khan: internal follow-ups: 1) update runbook to include auto session cap, 2) add anomaly alert for per-tenant streaming session surge, 3) schedule a post-incident review with Eng/ML/CSE next Tue.
Priya Nair: I'll add telemetry-based guardrails and the repro notes to the internal RCA doc.
Linh Tran (CSE): I've opened ticket REM-4871 for the customer comms and attached the draft. Also scheduled a sync with Vermilion engineers for Mon 10:00 UTC to walk through payloads and staging replay.
IncidentBot: Reminder: oncall handoff in 10m. Alex, do you want to do formal handoff?
Alex Reyes: handing off to Priya for monitoring. Priya, if error >2% re-escalate to Jamal and page Eng-ML.
Priya Nair: acknowledged. I'll keep dashboards in the morning and post RCA link when ready.
Hannah Park (Billing): billing flagged: pre-approve 15% credit pending finance confirmation. please cc billing@redwood when sending final comm.
Linh Tran (CSE): Sent customer update (ticket VL-2219). pasted message into ticket and included proposed credit. Vermilion replied: thanks, want the RCA and a timeline for the permanent fix.
Jamal Khan: timeline: patch -> staging canary tomorrow, full rollout next maintenance window (TBD) unless Vermilion requests expedited path. Priya and Alex to coordinate.
Priya Nair: closing notes: reproducer present, PR #902 linked, runbook change submitted, monitoring alert added.
Linh Tran (CSE): nice response from customer, they'll provide payload samples for staging. scheduling follow-up.
IncidentBot: Thread manually resolved by Alex Reyes at 09:45 UTC.
